requirements: Port exact upstream empty-root, leaf/node/root literal vectors and ten happy-path inclusion/consistency vectors. Retain exact commit/path/copyright/licence provenance. Null Go proof arrays mean empty arrays.
Proof JSON inputs are already hashed leaf/root bytes encoded as base64; leaf-data constants instead exercise leafHash over raw data. Keep the layers distinct.
Use node:crypto directly for a naive recursive tree over deterministic distinct binary data; do not call AMC hashing/root helpers to compute expected values.

Cross-check every size 1..64, every inclusion index and every consistency pair 0<=m<=n, plus the empty root. Verify generated proofs against independently calculated roots. Retain exact external proof paths separately so shared generator/verifier errors cannot make the only oracle pass.

Require false for malformed non-lowercase/non-64-hex verification hashes, invalid safe-integer/range inputs, tampered leaf/root/proof hash, a discriminating wrong index, and concrete extra/missing path cases, each after valid positives.

Use the dedicated size2-to-size3 proof witness from controls.json; never generalize it to all alternate declared sizes. Low-level nodeHash/rootHash are typed helpers, not a newly invented malformed-input throwing API.
AMC entryLeafHash consumes the raw32 bytes of an entry hash; rootHash consumes already hashed leaves. Do not double-hash either vector family.

Exercise both legacy and RFC adapters and finite frontier roots/shapes. RFC verification derives sides from index/size and ignores display-only position flags; signed-root authority remains a caller responsibility.
Show [a,b,c] and [a,b,c,c] share the legacy root but have different RFC roots using deterministic distinct entry hashes.
Verify existing legacy proofs with existing legacy APIs; no deletion, rewrite or migration of legacy data.
